text.p: Jefferson-Pilot Corp said on Tuesday it has completed the acquisition of Chubb Life Insurance Co of America and its subsidiaries from Chubb Corp for $875 million.
The purchase price was paid by a $100 million dividend from Chubb Life to Chubb Corp and $775 million in cash from Jefferson-Pilot, the company said.

John Still, Jefferson-Pilot's senior vice president of corporate development, said the acquisition doubles the size of the company's life insurance business and broadens the product line with a variable universal life insurance policy.
Chubb Life, which has total assets of $5 billion, reported about $90 million in first year premiums in 1996, Still said.
Variable universal life insurance policies, a rapidly growing segment of the life insurance business, feature investment accounts with the insurance, Still said.
Chubb Corp said in a separate statement that it using proceeds from the sale to repurchase its common stock.
Jefferson-Pilot expects the deal to save $40 million in costs annually and that the deal should be accretive to the company's earnings per share about two years, Still said.
